benchmarks.name: Standard Single Target · Thrax Centurion Lv 9999 SP · 180 s · KPM
rules: The target is one Thrax Centurion at level 9999 on Steel Path. The fight lasts 180 seconds.
One target, so nothing here rewards clearing a room.
Every shot is aimed and lands on the weak point. The companion board removes the aim; between them they are the ceiling and the floor.
The score is kills per minute, counting the fraction of the current target already gone. Removing 3% of one target in 180 seconds scores 0.03 and still ranks.

Every main slot is filled, every evolution tier the entry has is taken, every arcane seat it has is filled. The Exilus slot is optional: a row may wear one and a row without one is not a lesser build, so the two sit on the same board and the better number wins.

The stance slot is optional too, and it is not a discount but a GRANT: a stance hands the weapon 10 mod capacity on a matching polarity, 5 on a bare slot and 4 on the wrong colour. A row without one is not a lesser build; it is a build that spent the capacity elsewhere.
Investment is not ranked: every entry is scored at full Forma, at max rank, and at the maximum roll of any bonus a player can raise by farming duplicates.
The reserve is not spent: every entry fires as if it were being resupplied, so nothing here ranks ammo economy. An entry that cannot be resupplied at all runs on its own reserve.

The melee weapon is DRAWN, not quick-melee: a card that says "With Melee Weapon Equipped" pays here. A build swung out of a gun is a different fight and the simulator has a switch for it; the ruler does not.
An entry that can be played more than one way is ranked once per way, and the way it was played is part of the row.

A buff starts the fight FULL only if it is permanent — no timer, and not spent by being used. Such a buff can be held for the whole engagement by anyone, so scoring it at anything less would rank how long ago the entrant last topped it up. Every other buff starts at zero and is earned in the fight. Two buffs in the data qualify today.
Nobody submits a number. A submission is a BUILD, and its score is computed here by this engine under the pinned seed above, so any row can be reproduced exactly by anyone with the repo.
benchmarks.standard: Standard means this fight is claimed to represent most play, not that it is the fight you play. The target is a Thrax Centurion because a build that beats it transfers: it belongs to no faction, so no faction mod and no faction bonus reads on it; it carries Overguard, which most Warframe abilities cannot take off, so the weapon has to; it is armoured and it is tanky; it is immune to no element, so every proc lands; its weak points are the ordinary ones, 3x on the head and 1x elsewhere; and killing it is what moves a mission along. Its flaws are stated rather than hidden — it carries no shield, its Overguard may sit high, and the spectral form it enters on death is switched off here. One target can still be over-fitted to, which is why the board keeps a deep field and not only its leader.

benchmarks.name: Demolisher · one target · Demolisher Devourer Lv 9999 SP · 4-player health · 180 s · KPM
rules: The target is one Demolisher Devourer at level 9999 on Steel Path, carrying the health a four-player squad gives it. The fight lasts 180 seconds.
ONE WEAPON FIRES. A four-player squad is a harder TARGET here, not three more guns — this arena has one shooter — so what is ranked is how much of that Demolisher your weapon alone takes off.
One target, so nothing here rewards clearing a room.
Every shot is aimed and every one lands on the weak point, which is worth 3x. This is the specialised fight, not the floor.
Radiation cannot proc on this unit: the type is dropped from the draw, and every other type on the build gets likelier for it.
It can never be Frozen, so Cold climbs to its cap and stays there. An Impact proc lands and counts as a status type, and does not stagger it.
The score is kills per minute, counting the fraction of the current target already gone. Removing 3% of one Demolisher in 180 seconds scores 0.03 and still ranks.

Every main slot is filled, every evolution tier the entry has is taken, every arcane seat it has is filled. The Exilus slot is optional: a row may wear one and a row without one is not a lesser build, so the two sit on the same board and the better number wins.

The stance slot is optional too, and it is not a discount but a GRANT: a stance hands the weapon 10 mod capacity on a matching polarity, 5 on a bare slot and 4 on the wrong colour. A row without one is not a lesser build; it is a build that spent the capacity elsewhere.
Investment is not ranked: every entry is scored at full Forma, at max rank, and at the maximum roll of any bonus a player can raise by farming duplicates.

The reserve is not spent: every entry fires as if it were being resupplied by the squad this target was brought for, so nothing here ranks ammo economy. An entry that cannot be resupplied at all runs on its own reserve.

The melee weapon is DRAWN, not quick-melee: a card that says "With Melee Weapon Equipped" pays here. A build swung out of a gun is a different fight and the simulator has a switch for it; the ruler does not.
An entry that can be played more than one way is ranked once per way, and the way it was played is part of the row.

A buff starts the fight FULL only if it is permanent — no timer, and not spent by being used. Such a buff can be held for the whole engagement by anyone, so scoring it at anything less would rank how long ago the entrant last topped it up. Every other buff starts at zero and is earned in the fight. Two buffs in the data qualify today.

Its nullifying pulse is not applied. The wiki describes it dispelling every Warframe ability within 6.5 m every five seconds; it does not do so in game today, and this simulation matches the game rather than the card — so Roar, Eclipse and Nourish are up here exactly as they are on the other boards.

the mines on its back are a 0.5x hitbox the sim never aims at — shots land on the body or the head, and a player would not choose the mines
it is not stopped or slowed here — a Cold status greatly slows a Demolisher in game (and is the one effect its pulse cannot cleanse), and this sim has no movement for that to matter to

enemies.name: Legacyte
unmodeled: its DAMAGE ATTENUATION is not applied here, and it is this unit's whole defence: the game caps what one instance and what one second can take off it, both as a share of its Max Health, so a build measured here removes far more of it than it would in game — the engine has the machinery and the constants are unpublished, so turning it on would be inventing the numbers rather than measuring them
its CAPPED STATUS VULNERABILITY is not applied: the game gives it a partial status immunity, and this roster has only the whole kind — a type either lands here or it does not
no weak point is published for it, so nothing on it is a head: a build that lives on headshots scores here as if every shot were a body shot
it gains additional random abilities with each generation, from a pool of more than twenty — a fight here is the same Legacyte every time

enemies.name: Techrot Babau
unmodeled: its tendril bulbs are a third hitbox the sim never aims at — shots land on the body or the head, and the bulbs answer a gun at 1.5x and a melee swing at 0.1x, which is a per-weapon-class multiplier this roster has no field for
it burrows and attacks from underground, and it drains health from what it hits — this arena has no movement to lose the target in and no player health to drain, so both are absent

unmodeled: 'successfully landing a tracer round grants a 20 second buff that adds 50% ABSOLUTE critical chance. This buff is retained on target death, and is not affected by mods' (wiki). It is a flat addition to the finished crit chance, granted by the OTHER firing mode, and this engine has no shape for a buff one mode grants another — so this entry fires at its own 23% where a player who has landed a beacon sits at 73%. It is the larger half of the weapon
the primary fire HOMES on a beaconed target for 20 seconds (wiki) — this arena's shots already go where they are aimed, so the homing buys nothing here and buys a great deal in a real room

the beacon's whole purpose is the +50% absolute critical chance and the homing it grants the PRIMARY fire, neither of which this engine can carry from one mode to another. Fired on its own it is a three-damage dart

unmodeled: the grenades are DETONATED BY HAND — 'it launches ballistic grenades that can be manually detonated with Alternate Fire', with no arming delay at all (wiki). This sim has no second trigger, so every grenade goes off the instant it lands, which is what a player detonating immediately gets and is therefore the ceiling. What is lost is the play pattern the weapon exists for: laying grenades and firing them together

only five grenades may be live at once, and multishot counts towards that limit (wiki) — so on this weapon a multishot mod buys fewer shots rather than more damage per shot, which is the one place multishot is not simply good. This sim resolves each shot on its own and never hits the cap

infinite_ammo: this weapon has no ammo reserve to run out of
melee_equipped: only a melee weapon can be swung without being drawn, so this weapon is always the one in your hands

unmodeled: the BATTERY DISCHARGE that fires when the magazine empties: a 20 m pulse for 100 Impact. It is now fully SPECIFIED and merely unbuilt — the page states its whole scaling rule and I had declared it unknowable: "This is affected by base damage, Faction Damage Bonus, and Firestorm / Primed Firestorm; but not by elemental or multishot bonuses." So: the base-damage bucket and the faction column reach it, elements and multishot do not, and its RADIUS takes the blast-radius mods the shot's own explosion refuses. Its status is a 100% CHANCE rather than a forced proc, so status mods push it past one proc and a negative-status riven makes it miss
the discharge also removes Sentient and Shadow Stalker damage resistances, which is worth nothing against any target in this roster — no Sentient here has one to strip
+30% Movement Speed while aiming, and the explosion's self-stagger: neither is a number this arena reads

the PURITY syndicate effect, which on a proc heals the wielder and nearby allies and cleanses status from them — the wielder is not a body in this arena and there are no allies, so it pays nothing
this weapon is SILENT and this arena has nobody to alert — stealth is worth nothing here and a great deal in a real mission

the embedded detonation also forces a RAGDOLL, which is not a damage type and is not applied here
